content: Taking estrogen, either alone or in combination with another hormone called progestin, can sometimes lead to serious side effects. These include an increased risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer), breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and blood clots. To reduce the risk of uterine cancer, your doctor may recommend taking a progestin as directed. The likelihood of these side effects depends on the dose of estrogen and the duration of its use. Therefore, it is important to use this medication at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest time necessary. Regular discussions with your doctor, ideally every 3 to 6 months, are essential to evaluate whether you still need to continue this treatment. If long-term use is required, annual physical exams, including breast exams, mammograms, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, should be conducted as directed by your doctor. This medication is a form of estrogen, a hormone used by women to alleviate symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to reduced estrogen production in the body. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist and follow the instructions carefully. Wash and dry your hands before handling the vaginal ring. Insert the ring high into the vagina as directed, and leave it in place for three months. After three months, remove and replace it with a new ring if treatment is to continue. Do not leave the ring in place for longer than three months. If inserted correctly, the ring should not be felt and will not interfere with sexual activity. If you feel discomfort or the ring falls out, rinse it with lukewarm water and reinsert it. To remove the ring, hook your finger through it and gently pull it out. If you have difficulty removing the ring, contact your doctor. Dispose of the used ring in the trash. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headaches, and weight changes. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. However, in rare cases, this medication can cause serious, potentially fatal complications, such as blood clots (leading to heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs) or toxic shock syndrome (a severe bacterial infection). Serious allergic reactions are also rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before using this medication, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco, as this increases the risk of blood clots, especially when using estrogen products. Inform your doctor if you have recently had or will have surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these situations also increase the risk of blood clots. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths, and use sunscreen. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. If you develop a vaginal infection while using the ring, you may leave it in place while treating the infection. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm the unborn baby. It also passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how this medication works or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses on this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. Store this medication at room temperature and do not remove the ring from its pouch until ready for use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Maintaining a healthy lifestyle, such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking, can help reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises, such as reading or solving puzzles, may help prevent dementia.
